description: vim.NIL is truthy userdata: JSON null from GitHub API decodes to vim.NIL (userdata), not nil. Since only nil and false are falsy in Lua, vim.NIL passes through all `or` fallbacks (x or 0, x or '') unchanged. In comments.lua, normalize_comment set line = raw.line or raw.original_line — when both were JSON null, this returned vim.NIL. The sort comparator then attempted vim.NIL < number, crashing with 'attempt to compare number with userdata'. Same bug latent in path field.
resolution: Always wrap API fields that may be JSON null with nil_if_vim_nil(value) helper (already exists in codebase). Apply to all nullable numeric and string fields in normalize functions, not just object fields. Pattern: `line = nil_if_vim_nil(raw.line) or nil_if_vim_nil(raw.original_line)`.

description: `gh pr view --json files` has no `status` field: The `PullRequestChangedFile` GraphQL type does not expose file change status (added/modified/removed/renamed). The `gh pr view --json files` command returns only `path`, `additions`, `deletions`. Test mocks in tests/api/files_spec.lua fabricated a status field, masking the bug in CI. The crash was `attempt to index local 'status' (a nil value)` in normalize_status().
resolution: Either guard against nil status in normalize_status and default to 'modified', or switch from gh pr view --json files to gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/files --paginate (REST API returns actual status). Update all test mocks to reflect real API shape (no status field).

description: display_manager.attach() was dead code (now fixed): The function existed at manager.lua:85, passed unit tests, but was never called from any code path in the plugin. review.start() called display_manager.setup() (defines signs/highlights only) and controller.load() (fetches data into state) but nothing connected open buffers to the display system. Symptom: :Nit start fetched data but no signs appeared in buffers.
resolution: Fixed: try_attach_buffer() in review.lua calls display_manager.attach(bufnr, filepath) for all currently-open PR files after controller.load() stores threads into state. A BufEnter autocmd calls try_attach_buffer() when new PR files are opened during an active session.

description: Floating window focus lifecycle: nui popups lose focus silently when another window opens, or remain as ghost buffers after close. Neovim floating window focus behavior is inconsistent by design. The `focusable` attribute only controls :windo/CTRL-W navigation, not actual focus. Unmounting directly in BufLeave callbacks corrupts Vim state.
resolution: Use enter=true when mounting popups. Always wrap unmount calls in vim.schedule() to avoid state corruption. Set up BufLeave handler to unmount: `popup:on('BufLeave', function() vim.schedule(function() if popup and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(popup.bufnr) then popup:unmount() end end) end, { once=true })`. Verify window validity before operations: `if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(popup.winid) then return end`.

description: Buffer cleanup memory leaks: closing floating windows does not delete their buffers. Scratch buffers accumulate with :ls! showing growing unlisted buffers. If buffers contain folds, Neovim has a documented memory leak (issue #14040).
resolution: Set `bufhidden = 'wipe'` on popup buffers so they auto-delete when hidden. Also explicitly delete in cleanup: after popup:unmount(), call vim.schedule(function() if vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(bufnr) then vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(bufnr, { force=true }) end end). Track active_popup module variable and call close() before opening new popup.

description: State mutation race conditions: optimistic updates conflict with concurrent async responses. User resolves thread → local state updates → network takes 2s → user navigates → data refresh overwrites state → stale mutation response arrives and corrupts current state. Concurrent gh CLI calls can return out-of-order.
resolution: Track mutation_version counter. Increment on each mutation and on refresh. On mutation callback, check mutation_version == expected_version before applying; discard if stale. On failure, rollback only if still current version. Cancel all in-flight requests on controller.refresh().

description: GitHub secondary rate limit: rapid GraphQL mutations (resolve 5 threads quickly) trigger HTTP 403 for ~1 minute. GitHub requires ≥1 second between mutative requests (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE). The gh CLI does not automatically throttle.
resolution: Implement mutation queue with 1100ms minimum delay between consecutive mutations. Queue structure: table of {execute, callback} pairs, process sequentially with vim.defer_fn(process_mutation_queue, 1100) between each. Never fire mutations concurrently — always serialize through the queue.

description: mini.test async test concurrency: mini.test schedules all test cases via vim.schedule before any execute. If a test body calls vim.wait(), other scheduled test callbacks (including other tests and reporter.finish) fire concurrently, corrupting shared mock state (mock_system_results, mock_call_index). Symptom: only 1 test shows a pass indicator per file despite 10 cases collected.
resolution: Use synchronous tests in thread_panel_spec. For async mutations tests, each describe block gets its own local mock table (not shared), so mutations_spec.lua works reliably. Avoid adding new async tests to existing spec files that already have many async cases — add a new spec file instead.
